independent_thesis: Copart's auction liquidity, title workflows, logistics and permitted yards support continuing earning power, but weaker domestic service revenue and declining operating income contradict automatic compounding. Operating-equity DCF fits the claim; sum-of-parts is the strongest alternative, but requires allocation of shared customers, guarantees and upstream funding that the consolidated graph already reconciles. The latest parent balance-sheet quotation supports $1,907,901,000 cash including restricted cash and $2,581,901,000 held-to-maturity securities; the latter is not the separate securities-note total including interest receivable. Acquisition consideration is deducted once, target cash is accessibility-adjusted, and target shares never enter the parent denominator. ACVA's positive OCF is not treated as distributable finance earnings: software spending, compensation, credit losses and replacement lending capital remain charges. Main-case closure and matched maturation alternatives appropriately distinguish an investment phase from persistent losses. The weakest valuation inputs remain domestic activity persistence and realized yield, rather than acquisition recovery. Their declared bounds, adverse operating paths and measurable cash/revenue commitments make these explicit underwriting judgments. The two-year holding period leaves substantial realization dependence, but later spending, compensation and surviving claims remain projected through 2039.

inflation.reason: Nominal USD pricing, facility costs, purchased-vehicle costs, replacement capital and compensation have separate drivers. Positive incumbent revenue growth requires working capital, while declining revenue creates no automatic release. realization.reason: The two-year holding period is separate from the complete contractual projection and competitive continuation. Retained surplus is distributed once; restricted operating and claim reserves are not also added as terminal cash. Continuing lending preserves book capital and charges losses. Closure receives no invented asset recovery or legal discharge. The continuation uses earnings and incremental returns on a consistent parent-equity basis. Sources: doc_9b8366946fd8b140, doc_62c275106e3bc0df, doc_3f0da7f8c70b49fe, doc_c43b7db10ecff742.

largest_drivers.reason: This is the largest uncertainty, not an observed retention statistic. Recent domestic service weakness supports erosion, while owned yards, title workflows and buyer depth support slower deterioration. The model explicitly tests sustained 3% late activity losses and longer persistence with operating costs and capital requirements retained. The phase boundary is disclosed as judgment, and annual revenue/cash commitments can refute it.

Initial domestic activity normalization is separated from realized prices and international expansion. A severe multi-year activity contraction, pricing resistance and unavailable credit are tested together. The source does not identify precise unit retention, but the estimate is declared, bounded and falsifiable rather than presented as a financial fact.

Reported higher revenue per car alongside weaker domestic service revenue does not establish fee power. The model therefore separates controllable fees from realization and mix, applies fee elasticity, and independently stresses wages, purchased vehicles and replacement capital. Customer participation and revenue-per-car observations provide relevant review triggers.

diagnostic_resolutions.reason: The 84.632% exit-realization share is material and remains an investment risk. It largely reflects the independently chosen two-year holding period: trusted realization includes eleven further explicit annual bridges before the subsequent competitive continuation. Copart's continuing auction operations support a continuing claim, while FY2026 domestic weakness argues against assuming perpetual historical growth (doc_9b8366946fd8b140; obs_225c9f5d553432165c9b). Faster competitive erosion, persistent late activity and funding pressure, slower capital maturation, longer persistence, replacement inflation, compensation escalation and matched ACVA continuation/closure alternatives were tested. Later maintenance, growth funding and surviving claims remain charged, with no separate net-cash or hand-built operating exit added. These tests adequately expose the dependence; they do not establish persistence as fact.
